title: The `if` Statement: Making Decisions 🤔
description: Teach your script to react differently based on conditions – the first step to intelligent hacking tools.

slides.title: Your Script Needs a Brain 🧠
slides.content:
# From Linear to Smart

So far, your scripts run top to bottom. But hacking tools must decide: if a port is open, print "found"; if a login fails, try another password.

The `if` statement makes this possible. It runs a block of code only when a condition is `True`.

slides.title: Basic if Syntax
slides.content: The structure: keyword `if`, a condition, a colon `:`, then an indented block.
slides.codeSnippet:
port = 80
if port == 80:
    print("HTTP port is open!")
print("Scan continues...")

quizData.question: What happens if the condition in an `if` statement is `False`?
quizData.explanation: When the condition is false, Python jumps past the indented block.

slides.title: Condition: Any Boolean Expression
slides.content:
# The Heart of the if

The condition can be:
* Comparison: `port == 80`, `score > 100`
* Boolean variable: `is_vulnerable`
* Truthy/falsy values: `if username:` (runs if username is not empty)
* Logical combinations: `if port == 80 or port == 443`

Remember, it must evaluate to `True` or `False`.

quizData.question: `if 0:` will execute the block beneath it.
quizData.explanation: 0 is falsy, so the block is skipped.

slides.title: Indentation Matters (Again)
slides.content:
# All Lines in the Block Must Be Aligned

```python
if score > 90:
    print("Excellent!")
    print("You rock!")
print("Done")  # outside if
```
Inconsistent indentation causes `IndentationError`. Stick to 4 spaces.

slides.title: Common Mistake ⚠️
slides.content:
## Forgetting the Colon

```python
if port == 80   # SyntaxError: invalid syntax
    print("Open")
```
Always end the `if` line with a colon `:`.

slides.title: One‑Liner if (Not Recommended)
slides.content:
# You Can Squeeze It, but Don't

```python
if port == 80: print("Open")  # works, but ugly
```
For readability, always put the block on a new indented line. Readability = hackability.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Use `if` to Guard Against Errors

Before using a dangerous function, check input:
```python
if user_input.isdigit():
    port = int(user_input)
else:
    print("Invalid port")
```
This prevents `ValueError` crashes.
